queries.query_text: ClinicalTrials.gov phase III fecal microbiota transplantation immune checkpoint inhibitor solid tumor
Are there any registered Phase III randomized controlled trials evaluating fecal microbiota transplantation combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors in patients with solid tumors?

still_missing: Definitive confirmation of the absence or presence of *pure* Phase III randomized controlled trials (distinct from Phase II–III) registered in ClinicalTrials.gov or WHO ICTRP. The supplied material groups Phase II and III together ('4 were phase II–III trials') and does not explicitly confirm whether any trial met strict Phase III criteria. It also does not account for registry entries that may have been excluded from the meta-analysis due to lack of published results (the gap asks for ongoing or completed but unpublished trials).
usable_content: The study explicitly states that as of late 2025, 'no completed Phase III randomized trials have yet confirmed a reproducible survival benefit of microbiome-based interventions in oncology.' It identifies the current evidence base as relying primarily on Phase I/II trials (e.g., NCT03353402, NCT03341143 for FMT; NCT04167137 for SYNB1891; NCT03637803 for MRx0518) and meta-analyses. The text lists several ongoing early-phase trials involving microbiome interventions (FMT, defined consortia, engineered bacteria) combined with ICIs in solid tumors but does not identify any registered Phase III trials. It also mentions ongoing dietary intervention trials (e.g., NCT04645680) but classifies them as early-stage or observational. This study reports the MITRIC trial (NCT05286294), a single-arm phase IIa basket trial of FMT combined with ICIs in solid tumour patients (melanoma, HNSCC, RCC, pancreatic cancer). It explicitly states the trial design and registry number. The discussion mentions the randomized TACITO trial in metastatic RCC but does not specify its phase or registry identifier in the supplied text. This study conducted a systematic search of ClinicalTrials.gov, chictr.org, and major oncology conference abstracts up to September 30, 2024, using keywords 'Fecal' and cancer-related terms. It identified 10 studies involving 164 patients, of which 4 were classified as Phase II–III trials (e.g., NCT03686202, Spreafico et al. 2018) and 5 as Phase I trials. The authors explicitly state that larger-scale randomized controlled trials are required, implying a scarcity of completed Phase III data. The search strategy, date, and filters (no language or publication type filters initially) are documented.
